old_current_stem: This is _____ day of our week.
new_stem: Monday was _____ day last week.
reason: A completed last-week reference makes the comparison period explicit while leaving the article for the learner.

old_current_stem: At my home, this is _____ photo.
new_stem: This is _____ photo in our family album.
reason: The family album gives the photo a clear, familiar comparison set without pre-supplying the article.

old_current_stem: The zebra crossing is _____ the small road.
new_stem: Walking across at traffic lights is _____ walking across elsewhere on this road.
reason: This compares two crossing choices, and uses simpler traffic-lights wording instead of the less accessible zebra-crossing term.

old_current_stem: The bus is _____ the library.
new_stem: Our school bus is _____ our car.
reason: The revised B1 context compares two clearly described vehicles and uses natural possessives.

old_current_stem: Tom was _____ before the game.
new_stem: Before the game, Tom was _____ his brother.
reason: Naming Tom's brother makes the happiness comparison explicit.

old_current_stem: Ming was _____ Tom with the glass cups.
new_stem: Ming was _____ Tom when they carried glass cups.
reason: The parallel action makes clear that both boys were carrying the cups.

old_current_stem: Among students holding glasses, Ming is _____.
new_stem: Among students carrying glasses of water, Ming is _____.
reason: Glasses of water removes the possible spectacles meaning while keeping the superlative stem article-free.

old_current_stem: For our school, this is _____ idea.
new_stem: This is _____ idea for our school.
reason: The school reference now directly modifies idea, and the learner still supplies the article.

old_current_stem: The rain today is _____ yesterday's rain.
new_stem: Today's weather is _____ yesterday's weather.
reason: The context now compares weather rather than treating rain itself as worse.

old_current_stem: This is _____ weather this week.
new_stem: This is _____ weather we have had this week.
reason: The completed experiences within the current week make the comparison set clear.

old_current_stem: This is _____ bus ride this week.
new_stem: This was _____ bus ride I took this week.
reason: The past experience gives the bus-ride superlative a complete, natural reference.

old_current_stem: The shop is _____ the school is from my home.
new_stem: From my home, the shop is _____ the school.
reason: The shared distance reference is stated first.

old_current_stem: The park is _____ the school is from my home.
new_stem: From our home, the park is _____ the school.
reason: The common starting point is now explicit and uses a natural possessive.

old_current_stem: This bowl has _____ rice.
new_stem: Of four bowls, this one has _____ rice.
reason: The four-bowl set makes the quantity superlative unambiguous without pre-filling the article.

old_current_stem: Ming threw the ball _____ Tom.
new_stem: Ming threw the ball _____ Tom did.
reason: Did explicitly compares the two throwing actions.

old_current_stem: The bell rang _____ yesterday.
new_stem: The bell rang _____ it did yesterday.
reason: The repeated action makes the duration comparison explicit.

old_current_stem: Among teams, our team packed _____.
new_stem: Among teams, our team ran _____.
reason: Running is a more familiar and direct B1 action for this comparison.

old_current_stem: Tom studied _____ before the test.
new_stem: Tom studied _____ his brother did for the test.
reason: The sentence now explicitly compares the two boys' effort.

old_current_stem: In our class, Tom studied _____.
new_stem: Tom studied _____ in his class.
reason: The group phrase now sits naturally with the action while preserving both accepted adverb forms.

old_current_stem: The library opened _____ yesterday.
new_stem: The library opened _____ it did yesterday.
reason: Did makes the earlier-opening comparison explicit.

old_current_stem: Across school days, our library opened _____ on Monday.
new_stem: During our school week, our library opened _____ on Monday.
reason: School week provides a natural comparison period and avoids the awkward days phrasing.

old_current_stem: Our class started _____ the other class.
new_stem: Our lesson started _____ the other class's lesson.
reason: The revised parallel nouns make clear that lessons, not classes, began.

old_current_stem: In summer, the sun came up _____ in winter.
new_stem: In summer, the sun comes up _____ in winter.
reason: Present tense correctly presents the seasonal comparison as a general fact.

old_current_stem: Across all days, sunrise came _____.
new_stem: In my family, Dad gets up _____.
reason: A familiar family routine is clearer at B1 and has an explicit comparison group.

old_current_stem: Among teachers, our teacher spoke _____.
new_stem: Among our teachers, Mr Lee spoke _____.
reason: The named speaker and possessive group make the comparison specific and natural.

old_current_stem: Among buses, this bus came _____.
new_stem: Of these bus services, this one runs _____.
reason: Bus services and runs compare regularity rather than one arrival.

old_current_stem: Among students, Ming listened _____.
new_stem: Among students, Ming took our competition _____.
reason: This uses the natural take seriously collocation; our competition keeps the required superlative stem free of a literal article.

old_current_stem: Our team finished the game _____ last time.
new_stem: Our team played _____ it did last time.
reason: The pronoun did makes the earlier team performance explicit.

old_current_stem: Among teams, our team finished a game _____.
new_stem: Among all teams, our team completed this challenge _____.
reason: This names a shared task and gives successfully a clearer action without pre-filling the article.

old_current_stem: Among clocks, this clock showed time _____.
new_stem: Of these clocks, this one is set _____.
reason: Set correctly is the natural way to describe a clock's time setting.

old_current_stem: Our blue card was marked _____ of all.
new_stem: Of our cards, rain damaged this blue card _____.
reason: The new physical-damage context lets every existing badly superlative form fit naturally.

old_current_stem: Among students, I worked _____.
new_stem: Of everyone in my class, I worked _____.
reason: The retry now has a complete, article-free class comparison set while retaining the existing accepted forms.
